run.question: A customer reported an order failure with trace ID TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR. Can you search across all our app-190-service-* indexes to trace the request flow and find where the error originated? What error code was returned?

report.summary: The trace ID TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR is present in the four app-190 log indices (auth, gateway, inventory, orders), which are the only indices in the Elasticsearch target. Six log documents carry that trace_id in the 2026-11-23 16:52:14–17:52:14Z window, spanning 17:26:00.000Z to 17:26:00.140Z and describing one order attempt by user_12847 for SKU-78234, quantity 500: gateway received POST /api/orders, auth authenticated the user, orders began processing, and then inventory logged ERROR INV-ERR-4082 'Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23'. The error propagated back as orders ERROR ORD-ERR-1001 ('inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082') and surfaced at the edge as gateway ERROR GW-ERR-400 'Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled'. The origin of the failure is therefore the inventory service's stock reservation, rejected because only 23 units were available against 500 requested; the code returned to the caller at the gateway was HTTP 400 with error code GW-ERR-400 (internal propagation code ORD-ERR-1001, originating code INV-ERR-4082). Within the same one-hour window there are exactly three ERROR-level documents across all four indices — one per service in gateway, orders and inventory — and all three belong to this trace; auth logged 51 INFO and zero coded errors. This is a single-request business-condition failure, not a burst: no other error code appears in the window. Jaeger could not be used to cross-check the request graph (the supplied trace ID is not a hexadecimal Jaeger trace ID and the app-190 service names are not in that Jaeger service list, which is the otel-demo stack), Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every query, and no Kubernetes objects exist for the auth/gateway/inventory/orders services, so no span graph, metric rate or pod-level status corroborates the log-only view.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch target holds exactly four app-190-service-* indices — app-190-service-auth (51 docs), app-190-service-gateway (52), app-190-service-inventory (51), app-190-service-orders (52) — and a wildcard index listing returned only these four, all green/open.

All four indices map the fields @timestamp (date), duration_ms (integer), error_code (keyword), level (keyword), message (text), service (keyword), span_id (keyword) and trace_id (keyword), so trace_id is an exact-match keyword field.

A search of app-190-service-* for trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR returned exactly 6 documents (total relation eq, 6 = all of them shown), ordered in time: auth span-auth-err at 17:26:00.010Z "User user_12847 authenticated via JWT token" (15 ms, INFO); gateway span-gw-err at 17:26:00Z "Received request POST /api/orders for user_12847" (2 ms, INFO); orders span-orders-err at 17:26:00.030Z "Processing order for product SKU-78234, quantity: 500" (25 ms, INFO); inventory span-inv-err at 17:26:00.080Z (45 ms, ERROR); orders span-orders-err-2 at 17:26:00.130Z (130 ms, ERROR); gateway span-gw-err-2 at 17:26:00.140Z (145 ms, ERROR).

The originating error document is in app-190-service-inventory: level ERROR, error_code INV-ERR-4082, service inventory, span_id span-inv-err, message "Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23" at 2026-11-23T17:26:00.080Z, duration_ms 45.

The orders service logged error_code ORD-ERR-1001 in span span-orders-err-2 with message "Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082" (2026-11-23T17:26:00.130Z, duration_ms 130), and the gateway logged error_code GW-ERR-400 in span span-gw-err-2 with message "Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled" (2026-11-23T17:26:00.140Z, duration_ms 145) — both explicitly attributing failure to the inventory error.

In the same one-hour window (2026-11-23T16:52:14Z–17:52:14Z) the four indices contain 206 documents and only 3 ERROR-level documents: gateway 1 ERROR (GW-ERR-400) of 52, orders 1 ERROR (ORD-ERR-1001) of 52, inventory 1 ERROR (INV-ERR-4082) of 51, auth 0 errors of 51 (all INFO, no error_code bucket); no other error_code values exist in the window.

The Kubernetes cluster at query time ran 32 pods, all in kube-system, local-path-storage or otel-demo (e.g. frontend, checkout, cart, product-catalog, payment); no pod or workload named auth, gateway, inventory or orders was present, so pod status, restart counts and container logs are not available for the four services that appear in the app-190 log indices.

Rejected: the failure originated in the gateway or in the orders service as their own defect. Both services' error documents state the cause verbatim as the inventory error — orders "inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082" and gateway "400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled" downstream of that — and each service has exactly one ERROR document, which is the propagation of this single request.

Rejected: authentication caused the failure. The auth document in this trace is INFO level with no error_code ("User user_12847 authenticated via JWT token"), and the aggregation over the window shows 51 INFO / 0 ERROR and an empty error_code bucket for the auth service.

The proximate cause of the order failure is a stock-availability condition rather than a runtime or infrastructure fault: inventory rejected the reservation because the requested quantity (500) exceeded what was available (23) for SKU-78234. The log message states a business shortfall and no exception, timeout or connectivity error is present on any span of the trace.

Confirm with the inventory data owners whether SKU-78234 genuinely had only 23 units available at 2026-11-23T17:26:00Z (a stock/back-order situation) rather than a catalogue or stock-count synchronization problem; the logs do not distinguish those two, and only the business data can.

If the client needs a machine-readable HTTP status rather than the internal codes, note that GW-ERR-400 is recorded with HTTP 400 Bad Request at the gateway; consider whether a 409/422-style semantic is preferable for insufficient-stock rejections, and add the inventory code to the client-facing payload so callers see INV-ERR-4082 directly.

gaps: Jaeger could not corroborate the trace graph: traces_query_trace_by_id with TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR returned INVALID_PARAMS (the ID is not a hexadecimal Jaeger trace ID), traces_search for service "inventory" returned INVALID_PARAMS (inventory is not one of the Jaeger services, which are the otel-demo names such as frontend, checkout, product-catalog), and traces_list_services later returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE — so no span-level parent/child graph, no span counts and no per-operation latency exist for this request.

Prometheus was unreachable for every query in this Run: metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query (including a bare 'up') and get_metric_names all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so there is no error-rate, request-rate or latency baseline for the auth, gateway, inventory or orders services, and no comparison of the 45/130/145 ms spans against normal latency (no latency trend is asserted).

No Kubernetes objects exist for the auth, gateway, inventory or orders services (the cluster holds only the otel-demo stack), so pod status, container last-termination reasons, restart counts, events and application stderr/stdout for these services are unchecked; 'insufficient inventory' could not be checked against any stock service or database.

The four app-190 indices contain only 51–52 documents each, all inside the 16:52:14–17:52:14Z query window; whether the same trace appears outside that window, or whether earlier attempts for SKU-78234 failed, is unknown because the time filter could not be widened beyond the authorized window.
Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so whether a deployment, configuration change or stock-data load preceded the 17:26:00Z failure cannot be determined.
Elasticsearch document counts and index health are point-in-time readings taken at 17:52Z, after the incident; they cannot prove index state during the failure.
next_steps: Ask the inventory/data team for the stock record of SKU-78234 at 2026-11-23T17:26:00Z to confirm whether 23 available units was a true stock level or a synchronization error.

Once Prometheus is reachable, check inventory/orders/gateway error ratios and request latency around 2026-11-23T17:26:00Z against an earlier baseline to confirm the failure is isolated to this trace as the logs suggest.

If span-level confirmation is required, re-run the trace lookup in the APM/Jaeger instance that actually instruments the app-190 services (auth, gateway, inventory, orders), since the registered Jaeger target only holds the otel-demo services.

view.cannot_prove: This is the state at the moment of the query only: it cannot prove which indices, fields or document counts existed during the incident window, nor that any document lies in that window. A field that is mapped is not proof that documents carry it.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
